If your AI assistant is still asking for permission before every minor task, its system prompt is already outdated.

As LLMs transition from chat interfaces to autonomous agents, the way we instruct these models is shifting rapidly.

Here is what is changing in the development landscape today:

🤖 Anthropic has updated the system prompt for Claude Code to enforce autonomous execution. The new instructions explicitly tell the model that the user is not watching in real-time, preventing it from blocking work with questions like "Want me to...?" or "Shall I...?".

🛠️ A new tool called Claudette has gained traction, reaching 213 points on Hacker News. The project, hosted under the "nobuzz" repository, is designed to strip away verbose filler and stop Claude from writing in an overly conversational, BuzzFeed-style tone.

🎮 Google DeepMind is expanding its 15-year history of gaming research, which spans from Atari to EVE Online. The organization is now partnering directly with game studios to prototype new gameplay mechanics.

🥞 A Google DeepMind engineer has released a framework defining "full-stack" AI. The guide breaks the development stack down into five distinct layers to help developers and users navigate the ecosystem.

The trend is clear: we are moving away from chatty, hand-holding assistants and toward quiet, autonomous execution at every layer of the stack.

Do you prefer autonomous agents that execute tasks silently, or do you still want step-by-step confirmation?
